answer: A verifier peer issues each identity a micro-benchmark with a hard wall-clock deadline, say 90 seconds to train a small sonnet head on a sharded kernel trace and return loss plus weight hash. Because the clock starts at dispatch and the response must land before a signed comet nonce on the peer's own ledger, a clone cannot queue the job behind other clones on one GPU and return later; time-sharing across N identities forces N concurrent slots, and each slot needs real VRAM.
